In consideration of the Borrower’s commitment to assist the University by developing, financing, constructing, owning and operating the Student Housing Facilities for the benefit of the students, faculty and staff of the University, the Board of Trustees is willing to make certain commitments to the Project as set forth herein; NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing recitals, the covenants and agreements set forth hereinafter, and othe r good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1.
Ground Lease .
Pursuant to the Ground Lease, the Borrower shall acquire a leasehold interest in the Property from the Univer sity and thereafter design, develop, finance, construct, own and operate the Project as contemplated by the Ground Lease.
Capitalized terms used herein without definition shall have the meaning given in the Ground Lease, or if not defined therein, in the Management Agreement.

On the date hereof, Borrower is entering into a property management agreement (“Management Agreement”) with WGB Property Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company doing business as Inwood Management (the “Manager”) for the management of the Project as more particularly described in the Management Agreement, subject to the University’s rights and obligations described in Section 3 below. 2.
Responsibility Matrix .
Upon Substantial Completi on of the Student Housing Facilities, the Borrower shall operate, or cause to be operated, all such improvements solely as student housing and related facilitie s, serving Residents in accordance with the Responsibility Matrix attached hereto as Exhibit A (“ Responsibility Matrix”).
The University shall assume all obligations and responsibilities of the University as set forth in the Respon sibility Matrix and/or the Management Agreement.
In the event of an inconsistency between this Agreement and the Responsibility Matrix, the Responsibility Matrix sha ll govern.

Unless otherwise stated in this Agreement, the Management Agreement or shown in the Annual Budget, all costs incurred by the University for any of the University’s obligati ons under this Agreement shall not be a Program Expense and the University shall not be entitled to reimbursement for any of such costs. 3.
Operation of New Undergraduate Housing Projects .
The University shall support the New Undergraduate Housing Projects by doing the following in connection with this Agreement: a.
Housing Agreements.
The University shall in the ordinary course of business, enter into Housing Agreements with Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects pursuant to a form of Housing Agreem ent consistent with the form of Housing Agreements utilized for the University’s othe r undergraduate housing.
The University shall enforce compliance by each Resident with his or her Housing Agreement consistent with the terms of said Housing Agreement and University housing policies. b.
Resident Collections.

The University shall use diligent efforts to demand, collect (or cause to be collected) and receive: (a) all Gross Fees due a nd payable from Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, (b) all other pass-through or bill-back charges, sums, costs or expenses of any nature whatsoever payabl e by third parties relating to all or any portion of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, (c ) all other General Revenues accruing from occupancy or use of, activities at, or services provided for Residents at the New Undergraduate

3 4927-7091-6163.5 Housing Projects, and (d) all Behavioral Fees, if any, from Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
The University will maintain and diligently enforce with respect to the Student Housing Facilities its then-current policies in the event of delinquencies in the payment of Resident fees under Housing Agreements. c.
Resident Application and Selection Process.
With respect to Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, the University will manage and administer the housing application and lease up process for the New Un dergraduate Housing Projects during the Term, including, without limitation, the procedures for accepting housing applications from applicants, selecting Residents for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, making room assignments within the New Undergraduate Housing Projects , and facilitating student transfers between the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and any other housing on Campus, in each case in a manner consistent with its operation of other undergraduate housing on Campus. d.
Termination of Housing Agreements.

The University shall permit any Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to terminate his or her Housing Agreement pursuant to the terms of such Housing Agreemen t or as otherwise required by the Transaction Documents.
The University shall decide, ba sed on the terms and conditions of the Housing Agreement, when to terminate a Housing Agreement of any Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects who materially violates Univ ersity Policies or the terms of the Housing Agreement.
In the event that any Housing Agreement with respect to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects is terminated early, the University shall administer and manage the process of providing refunds to Residents (if applicable), the assessment of resident housing termination fees, and shall manage and supervise the physical move-out of the Resident from the New Undergraduate Housing Projects in which the Resident is residing. e.
Move-In and Move-Out.

With resp ect to the Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, the University shall coordinate and implement Resident move- in and move-out logistics, disseminate information to Residents about the move-in and move-out process, and provide custodial availability during all Resident move-in and Resident move-out periods. f.
Room Assignments and Transfers.
The University shall be responsible for assigning each Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to a particular unit within the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, as available. g.
Custodial Services.
The University shall provide custodial services at the New Undergraduate Housing Projects consistent with the custodial services it provides at its other undergraduate housing on Campus and such services shall be maintained at a level of 1 to 2.9 under the APPA Standards.
The University shall procure all janitorial and custodial supplies to be used for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects. h.
Work Order Management.

The University shall coordinate with the Borrower and the Manager to assist Manager in developing a work order management system that is integrated with the University’s student housing work order management system.

Damage by Residents.
The Manager shall assess and determine any and all damages to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects beyond reasonable wear and tear caused by any Resident or such Resident’s guests.
Based on such assessment and determination of damages by the Manager, the University shall invoice any such Resident in a New Undergraduate Housing Project for the costs to repair any such damage for which such Resident is responsible in accordance with a damages and billing sheet, the form of which has been mutually agreed upon by the Manager, Borrower and University.
The Univ ersity shall collect any funds that a Resident may be obligated under the applicable Housing Agreement to pay for such damage. j.
Recycling and Waste Hauling.
The Housing Agreements will provide that residents are responsible for taking trash and items to be recycled to designated trash areas within the Student Housing Facilities containing separate trash and recycling bins.

The University shall remove trash and items to be recycled in th e common areas of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to such designated trash areas for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, and the Manager will remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the Graduate Housing Project to such designated trash areas for the Graduate Housing Project.
The University shall arrange for the pickup of such trash and recycling from all of such designated trash areas for all of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to contracts between the University and third-party contractors, which expenses shall be Program Expenses to be reflected on the Annual Budget (as defined in the Ground Lease) and reimbursed to the University per the Annual Budget. k.
Landscaping and Snow Removal.
The Un iversity shall be responsible for all landscaping and snow removal on the Campus including, but not limited to, the Student Housing Facilities and parking lots.

The University shall be reimbursed as a Program Expense for such snow removal from the areas between the line th at is twenty feet from the exterior doors of the Student Housing Facilities to the adjacent parkin g areas, as more particularly detailed in the Responsibility Matrix, provided such expenses are within the Annual Budget. l.
No Adverse Effect on Bonds.
The University shall not take any action with respect to the Project that would adversely affe ct the exemption of interest on the Bonds from gross income for federal tax purposes or would otherwise result in a breach of any representations, conditions, or covenants of Borrower as set forth in the Bond Documents. l.
No Competing Projects.

The Universi ty agrees to not undertake to build, invest in, finance, lease, own (in whole or in part), operate or market any new Competing Facility unless (A) the construction of the Competing Fa cility is supported by a demand study from an independent consultant dated not more than eighteen (18) months prior to the projected construction date, concluding that sufficient demand exists for the additional number of beds to be constructed so as not to have a material adverse effect on the Project and (B) the Senior Debt Service Coverage Ratio (as such term is defined in the Trust Agreement) for the two most recently ended Annual Periods (as such term is defi ned in the Trust Agreement) was at least 1.20.
The projections and demand study shall be prepared by a nationally recognized consulting firm experienced in student housing selected by th e University and approved by Borrower, in Borrower’s reasonable discretion.
A “Competing Facility” as used herein means student housing facilities marketed primarily to students of the University’s Campus.

The term “ Competing Facility” shall exclude the replacement or renovation by the University of any current on-Campus student housing facility, as long as the number of beds in the replacement student housing facility

Project Support Generally .
The University shall support the Student Housing Facilities by doing the following in connection with this Agreement: a.
Marketing.

Support the marketing of the Student Housing Facilities by: (i) offering the New Undergraduate Housing Pr ojects as an on-campus housing option for its undergraduate students; (ii) including the Student Housing Facilities in pertinent information and marketing materials regarding student housing that it provides to students and prospective students, including providing information about the Stude nt Housing Facilities on the University website; (iii) allowing the Borrower to advertise the availability of the Graduate Housing Project on the University’s campus and website, including providing a link to apply for housing within the Graduate Housing Project; (iv) referring or otherwise promoting the availability of the Student Housing Facilities to students seeking housing in the same manner as its own housing facilities, as applicable. b.
University Services.
Provide students residing at the Project the same services and access it provides to admitted students, including without limitation, the University’s current student life programs, access to the University’s online resources and student transportation system, if applicable. c.
No Preferential Assignment.

Not to dir ect or assign students on a priority basis to other student housing facilities in preference over the Project unless: (i) such actions are necessary, in the sole judgment of the University, to address a new outbreak of a widely reported, contagious pathogen, whether viral, bacterial or otherwise causing a local or regional epidemic or pandemic; or (ii) to meet the University’s special programmatic needs, such as housing for residential learning communities, athletes or honors programs. d.
Campus Security.
To the extent permitted by law, ensure that the Project will be subject to the jurisdiction of the University’s campus security force.
The University’s campus security force shall have the right to access the Student Housing Facilities as necessary to perform its duties in accordance with University Policies, including the right to access security camera footage. e.
Information Technology.

Provide for use at the Project, in the same quality and manner as provided in the University’s other Campus housing, information technology equipment, including servers, racks and related devices for the provision of University WiFi, to be housed in locked IT closets provided by Borrower within the Project.
For the Graduate Housing Project, the University, Borrower, and Manager will implement a communications fee to be paid by residents of the Graduate Housing Project and delivered to the University to offset the cost of such information technology equipment.
Funds r eceived by the University as payment of such communications fee shall not constitute General Revenues.

Parking.
Provide Residents and employees of the Manager with access to University parking permits which will give them access to campus parking, including any nearby parking facilities, with the same priority and contract terms granted to other students, faculty, staff and affiliates of the University; g.
Continuing Disclosure.
To the extent allowable by law and subject to the Borrower or Manager obtaining necessary waiv ers and consents from the residents where necessary, using commercially reasonable efforts to assist the Borrower with its continuing disclosure obligations related to the Bonds, providing Borrower with such information about the University or the Project that the Borrower is required to provide in order to comply with any such continuing disclosure obligations, including de mographic and statistical information about the University’s enrollment and on-campus housing; h.
